newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreigners boost Nairobi bourse index, turnover.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners boost Nairobi bourse index, turnover.

text.p: Foreign demand for key shares in the market sustained the upward movement of the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index on Tuesday in a very active market, brokers and bourse officials said.
The index went up 10.80 points to stand at 3164.01 points.
Turnover was posted at 43.490 million shillings traded on 1,239,581 shares from 16.118 million shares on 316,265 shares.
Brokers said activity had definitely picked up in the market as there was demand in almost all counters.
"Give it this week, by the end of next week most prices should have gone up by three to five shillings," a broker said.

Foreigners bought 83,264 shares of Kenya Power & Lighting at a reserve price of 165 from 144, 720,000 shares of Kenya Airways at 8.50 from 8.85 and 139,000 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at between 78 and 80 from 75.

Another broker said the government element in the power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co did not appear to discourage investors. "Kenya Power is one of those shares in the market that has been on the upper side for the last twelve months."
Some brokers said the turnaround in a Kenya Airways share price was due to positive publicity surrounding the airline pushing it as a good medium to long term investment.

The airline's price was adversely affected by industrial disputes within it and postponement of the election of board of directors. The price went to an all-time low of 7.0 as disappointed speculators panicked and sold their shares.
In the financials, Barclays Bank gained one to close at 102, while National Bank of Kenya traded at 15.10 from 14.15.
Rea Vipingo Plantations closed at 10 unchanged, while Uchumi Supermarket closed at 54.50 unchanged.
